description: Vocoder from Surge: a bank of filters follows the spectrum of the modulator input and imposes it on the carrier input.

params.text: Sets the output level of the vocoder, -48dB to 48dB.
Sets the level below which a filter band is silenced, -96dB to 0dB.
Sets how quickly each band's envelope follower tracks the modulator, 0 to 100%.
Sets how sharp the filter bands are, -100% to 100%.
Scales both carrier inputs before the vocoder, from silence to unity gain.
Scales both outputs after the effect, from silence to unity gain.
Scales both modulator inputs before the vocoder, from silence to unity gain.

inputs.text: The left carrier input, the signal the filter bands shape; with the right carrier input unpatched this one feeds both channels.
The right carrier input, the signal the filter bands shape.
Adds to the Gain / Level knob, a tenth of its full range per volt.
Adds to the Gate / Level knob, a tenth of its full range per volt.
Adds to the Rate / Filter knob, a tenth of its full range per volt.
Adds to the Q / Filter knob, a tenth of its full range per volt.
The left modulator input, the signal whose spectrum is followed; with the right modulator input unpatched this one feeds both channels.
The right modulator input, the signal whose spectrum is followed.

outputs.text: The left output of the effect; with the right output unpatched this one carries an even mix of the two channels.
The right output of the effect.

notes: two signals are needed before anything comes out: a carrier into the audio inputs, which the filter bands shape, and a modulator into the modulator inputs, whose spectrum they follow.
the effect runs in blocks of 32 samples, so it delays the signal by 32 samples and reads its CV inputs once per block.
this module is deprecated and hidden in the module browser; the Surge XT plugin replaces it, and both plugins can be used in one patch.
menu: Skins — a submenu of four colour schemes, listed by file name as Classic.xml, Miami.xml, NewYork.xml and Night.xml; picking one repaints every Surge module in the rack.
